3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: The door swung open and Lucian Galade, my chief strategist, walked in. He was a compact man with sharp, birdlike features. After briefly surveying the room from wall to wall, he sat down, poured a glass of water and opened his briefcase in a series of quick, graceful movements.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: Petr Vectern arrived a couple of minutes early and sat across from me. He was struggling to hold back his smile.

5.speaker: Petr Vectern
5.text: “But, hey, back in university, did you ever imagine we would be sitting here in the Maroon Palace? We have to celebrate this great victory.”

6.speaker: Player
6.text: “This is not the time to celebrate, Petr. We have work to do.”

7.speaker: Player
7.text: “We will celebrate at the inaugural ball. Just hang in there until the evening.”

8.speaker: Player
8.text: “Let's celebrate then. I got my hands on something special for us. An Erlory Maroon 30-year-old.”

9.speaker: Petr Vectern
9.text: “Looking forward to it. Evelyn hopes to congratulate you in person there.”

10.speaker: Player
10.text: “Good to know. It's been some time since the last time I saw her."

11.speaker: Player
11.text: “I'm sure the kids would love to see their Uncle Petr for the first time as the Vice President.”

12.speaker: Petr Vectern
12.text: “I think it was Franc's birthday. We've barely had enough time for our families over these past months, haven't we?”

13.speaker: Petr Vectern
13.text: “That is great to hear! It's crazy how fast the two have grown up. You are a good father.”

14.speaker: Narrator
14.text: Petr had a wistful look in his eyes. He and Evelyn had never been able to have kids of their own. During our campaign, the opposition had floated the rumor that he'd fathered illegitimate children during his wilder years, but it had never been substantiated.

15.speaker: Petr Vectern
15.text: “Yes... I agree. We've got things to do today. We can let loose at the ball.”

17.speaker: Petr Vectern
17.text: “We'll be talking about our political strategy for this term. Lucian and I had a meeting with the party and the reformists."

18.speaker: Petr Vectern
18.text: “We mostly see eye to eye, but I would want to know what you think.”

19.speaker: Player
19.text: “Let's see if I see eye to eye.”

20.speaker: Player
20.text: “Great. Let's go over this when Lucian arrives.”

21.speaker: Narrator
21.text: The tall-case clock in the room struck three o'clock.

24.speaker: Narrator
24.text: Lucian then turned towards me. He very slightly bowed his head.

25.speaker: Lucian Galade
25.text: “Another important point. We must be aware of the Lotherberg Group. The Oligarchs convene under this organization to influence economic policies. Konrath Koronti led it for a long time before falling ill. The new leader is Mr. Walter Tusk."

26.speaker: Petr Vectern
26.text: “As far as I know, Konrath's son Marcel has strong ties to this group. His influence could definitely be an asset for us. But I'm sure he'll want something in return."

27.speaker: Player
27.text: “I am aware of Mr. Koronti's wide network. That could come in handy.”

28.speaker: Player
28.text: “The Group's influence is an important force. One that we should use to our administration's advantage.”

29.speaker: Player
29.text: “That group is dependent on our economic policies. They can't move a finger without us.”

30.speaker: Petr Vectern
30.text: “I wouldn't be so optimistic. The capital they represent could do a lot of damage if it was diverted.”

32.speaker: Player
32.text: “We'll see each other at the ball, then."

36.speaker: Lucian Galade
36.text: “According to reports, some members of the National Business Council are in their pockets. Tusk and the Group will surely try to bribe us in exchange for special economic protections.”

39.speaker: Petr Vectern
39.text: “If we can get them to side with us. It all depends on what benefits we can offer and what the leader wants."

40.speaker: Petr Vectern
40.text: “We just need to be careful with him. He looks like the lesser evil, but it could very quickly turn out to be the other way around.”

41.speaker: Lucian Galade
41.text: “We need to tread carefully on all sides with all power players to survive our term. I need to underline the seriousness of the situation.”

42.speaker: Lucian Galade
42.text: “This concludes our political briefing for today. Our next meeting will be about our media strategy.”

43.speaker: Narrator
43.text: Lucian and Petr bid their farewells and left. A mysterious amount of smoke was rising far away on the horizon.

44.speaker: Lucian Galade
44.text: “Let's start by evaluating our current situation."

45.speaker: Lucian Galade
45.text: “It may create issues for us, yes."

46.speaker: Lucian Galade
46.text: “However, with the reformists gaining more popularity, we may not be in a position to stand against them."

47.speaker: Lucian Galade
47.text: “The majority of the Sordish people demand change. They are more concerned about the economy than the Constitution, but they blame the system for their problems."

49.speaker: Petr Vectern
49.text: "People are losing their trust in our democracy. Why do you think radicals like Bernard Circas are becoming more popular? Everyone's expecting us to bring the change the last government did not."

50.speaker: Player
50.text: “I agree with the reformists. Our responsibility is to democratize our broken system."

51.speaker: Player
51.text: “We need to listen to the people if we want to serve this country."

52.speaker: Lucian Galade
52.text: “We will need many allies against the Old Guard in the government."

53.speaker: Player
53.text: “If we lose power, we won't be able to execute the changes we need to make for the good of the country."

57.speaker: Petr Vectern
57.text: "That's exactly what we campaigned for. A true change that will move the country forward."

60.speaker: Player
60.text: “Let's not waste any time. Lucian, proceed with the overview.”

61.speaker: Lucian Galade
61.text: “It is a privilege to be here, sir."

64.speaker: Lucian Galade
64.text: “A comprehensive reform that would make the reformists happy would mean maintaining a balance between all branches of government."

65.speaker: Petr Vectern
65.text: "I agree. The Old Guard won't like this, though."

66.speaker: Petr Vectern
66.text: "We need to work with the Supreme Court one way or the other."

67.speaker: Lucian Galade
67.text: “Which means removing your absolute veto as well. The reformists demand that all loopholes in the Constitution are closed."

68.speaker: Player
68.text: “We'll need a comprehensive bill to balance the power structure more fairly."

69.speaker: Lucian Galade
69.text: “The Old Guard will do its best to preserve the Constitution. Chief Justice Hawker and his allied judges have a great influence over the Supreme Court, which will be tough to break."

70.speaker: Lucian Galade
70.text: “Mr. Ricter managed to persuade many members of Assembly to give their support for drafting a new Constitution. Reformist politicians are quickly increasing in number."

71.speaker: Petr Vectern
71.text: "The Court also has the final say over constitutional legislation. Without their approval, we cannot even change it."

72.speaker: Lucian Galade
72.text: “While the reformist wing inside our party is still a minority, they could have a tri-partisan majority in the assembly, especially if they unite under Frens Ricter."

73.speaker: Lucian Galade
73.text: “I agree. They have too much power over Sordish politics."

74.speaker: Player
74.text: “We must break the power of the Supreme Court one way or another."

75.speaker: Petr Vectern
75.text: "The reformists' demands are clear. They want to limit the President's veto powers, ensure that the Supreme Court is independent and take away the Court's right to vote on constitutional amendments."

76.speaker: Player
76.text: “I support the reformists. We need a proper balance of power in this country."

77.speaker: Player
77.text: “I'd rather not go against them. The risks are too high."

79.speaker: Lucian Galade
79.text: “True. But we can't let the Old Guard manipulate us and then backstab us, like they did with Alphonso."

80.speaker: Player
80.text: “We must listen to their demands. Otherwise we are no different than the previous administrations."

81.speaker: Player
81.text: "I won't allow them to influence me. We will shape our own future."

82.speaker: Petr Vectern
82.text: "We need to take away their vote in constitutional legislation. It is absurd that they get to vote for bills when they aren't even elected."

83.speaker: Petr Vectern
83.text: "I agree. We can't ignore the winds of change, after all."

84.speaker: Petr Vectern
84.text: “We can figure it out. Our party still holds 130 out of 250 seats in the Assembly. We've got the power."

86.speaker: Player
86.text: “Looks like we have many challenges ahead.”

88.speaker: Player
88.text: “We will write a more democratic Constitution with the reformists."

89.speaker: Player
89.text: “The new Constitution should give the President wide-ranging powers to lead Sordland into the future."

90.speaker: Player
90.text: “We could work with the Old Guard to protect our existing extensive powers."

94.speaker: Player
94.text: “How can we come out of this in the best shape?"

95.speaker: Petr Vectern
95.text: "That's what we've been preparing for internally. Don't forget that promise is what got us elected."

96.speaker: Lucian Galade
96.text: "The key thing here will be strengthening the power of the Assembly, which we already lead with a majority."

97.speaker: Player
97.text: “What do you suggest we do, then?"

98.speaker: Petr Vectern
98.text: "It will be tough to persuade our base if we work with Ricter and his band of reformists. But everyone agrees we need a new Constitution."

99.speaker: Player
99.text: “Cut it out, you two. Are you with me or not?"

100.speaker: Lucian Galade
100.text: “That will not be accepted by the reformists. This draft has been created with the advice of both our party and PFJP members."

101.speaker: Lucian Galade
101.text: "That's very bold. Then we must start with eliminating the Supreme Court's authority over constitutional legislation and perhaps take their immunity away."

102.speaker: Lucian Galade
102.text: “You would also be burning bridges with the Reformists and the Old Guard."

103.speaker: Petr Vectern
103.text: "Don't forget the reformists want us to address the loopholes in the presidential veto system."

107.speaker: Petr Vectern
107.text: "You must remember that we promised people a democratic Constitution during the elections."

108.speaker: Petr Vectern
108.text: "How? You know the public wants us to enact extensive reforms. And how do we know if the Old Guard would support you?"

110.speaker: Lucian Galade
110.text: "If we go against the demands of the people, the reformists will be furious. It could backfire."

112.speaker: Lucian Galade
112.text: "I don't think you should take the risk, Mr. President."

114.speaker: Player
114.text: “Only a strong administration can make Sordland great."

115.speaker: Player
115.text: “I will not limit my veto powers. We need them."

116.speaker: Lucian Galade
116.text: "Very well. We will begin to explore how to realistically pass such a constitutional change."

117.speaker: Player
117.text: “They can remain. Some reform is better than none."

118.speaker: Lucian Galade
118.text: “As you wish. We will move forward on that."

119.speaker: Player
119.text: “Of course, it will be looked at in detail."

120.speaker: Lucian Galade
120.text: "That is true, but if we don't evolve we might become part of the problem."

121.speaker: Lucian Galade
121.text: "However, I must stress that I am not for this."

123.speaker: Lucian Galade
123.text: “Second, the President's absolute veto will be taken away. This can be replaced with a limited veto system by fixing the current loopholes."

124.speaker: Player
124.text: “We must draft a bill to destroy the power of the judiciary."

125.speaker: Lucian Galade
125.text: “Taking away the legislative power of the Supreme Court while holding your own absolute authority over legislation would look like an attempt to consolidate your own power."

126.speaker: Petr Vectern
126.text: "Yes. The divisions of power need to be rebalanced for a better Sordland."

127.speaker: Player
127.text: "Fair enough. Let's work with the reformists."

128.speaker: Player
128.text: “We can handle it, just like the previous governments did."

129.speaker: Player
129.text: “True, we can't do it. It is too dangerous."

130.speaker: Player
130.text: "We must draft a bill with more executive powers."

131.speaker: Lucian Galade
131.text: "It is not a risk worth taking, Mr. President."

132.speaker: Player
132.text: "No, I will only support a new constitution that strengthens my position. Forget the reformists and reach out to the NFP instead."

133.speaker: Player
133.text: "Then I don't intend to pursue constitutional change. We will reach out to the Old Guard."

134.speaker: Lucian Galade
134.text: "It will be a dangerous path to follow."

135.speaker: Player
135.text: “I can handle them. It will be done under the Rayne administration."

136.speaker: Petr Vectern
136.text: "Why would you want to work with the Old Guard?"

137.speaker: Player
137.text: “Without the Sollists' support, we have no power."

138.speaker: Petr Vectern
138.text: "Keeping your absolute veto over legislation but taking away the Supreme Court's influence over the Assembly would make it look like a power grab."

140.speaker: Player
140.text: “We can do it, Lucian! Look at what we accomplished so far."

141.speaker: Lucian Galade
141.text: "The state is powerful as is. The question is how to approach these constitutional amendments and if it's realistic to pull off."

142.speaker: Petr Vectern
142.text: "You're talking about going against the reformists and public opinion all at once."

144.speaker: Lucian Galade
144.text: "I understand. We do not have to remove your veto. Instead, we can discuss limiting it with the reformists."

145.speaker: Petr Vectern
145.text: "I don't know if we can survive that politically."

146.speaker: Player
146.text: “What do you suggest we do then? Maybe I can reconsider working with the reformists."

147.speaker: Player
147.text: "No. This is not happening. I'd rather not include either of these points."

148.speaker: Player
148.text: "I want to minimize the damage to my seat."

149.speaker: Player
149.text: “I have no problems with these clauses. Let's work with the reformists."

150.speaker: Player
150.text: "The President needs to be able to exercise his powers with ease to maintain stability."

151.speaker: Player
151.text: "We must strengthen the state by removing the power of the Old Guard."

152.speaker: Player
152.text: “The real problem is the judiciary's power, not the president's."

154.speaker: Player
154.text: “We need to address other more important problems, too."

155.speaker: Player
155.text: “What is the best outcome for us then?"

156.speaker: Lucian Galade
156.text: "If you are serious about this, I will explore the options for you, Mr. President."

157.speaker: Lucian Galade
157.text: “To clarify before we head in any particular direction, what are your intentions, sir?"

158.speaker: Lucian Galade
158.text: “The public might be persuaded, but the reformists in the Assembly are not going to fall for that."

159.speaker: Lucian Galade
159.text: “They would try to paint you as yet another strongman trying to grab more power for himself."

161.speaker: Lucian Galade
161.text: "It would be quite difficult to secure the 166 votes needed to propose such a bill."

163.speaker: Petr Vectern
163.text: "It will be very difficult to plead that case to the reformists."

167.speaker: Petr Vectern
167.text: "Anton, we got elected by promising democratic reforms."

168.speaker: Lucian Galade
168.text: “That would be tough, sir. But I trust your judgement."

170.speaker: Petr Vectern
170.text: "That does include strengthening the Assembly by giving them a chance to override vetoes, as well as ensuring that the judiciary is independent."

171.speaker: Player
171.text: "We don't need the reformists. We can always work with the NFP."

172.speaker: Lucian Galade
172.text: “As you wish. We will move forward on that."

173.speaker: Player
173.text: “We can package it as a *democratic* reform.”

174.speaker: Lucian Galade
174.text: “However, most people will not be persuaded by that. It would be tough to reach the 166 votes needed to propose such a bill."

175.speaker: Player
175.text: “You're right. Let's work with the reformists."

176.speaker: Player
176.text: “No matter what you say, I intend to come out of this stronger as the President.”

177.speaker: Lucian Galade
177.text: "Well... Let's see what we can do about it."

179.speaker: Petr Vectern
179.text: "What everyone's expecting is a rebalance of power between the executive, legislative and judiciary branches."

180.speaker: Petr Vectern
180.text: "Of course. We'll have time to discuss everything you want."

181.speaker: Player
181.text: “If it must be done, I will do it."

182.speaker: Petr Vectern
182.text: "The reformists are pretty loud about their thoughts on the presidential powers, Anton. You know they think this position breeds dictators."

184.speaker: Lucian Galade
184.text: “According to the initial draft we made with the reformists, there are two changes to the Constitution that are not open for their discussion."

185.speaker: Player
185.text: “I see that. But we will move towards this direction for now."

186.speaker: Player
186.text: “I don't care what they think. We can handle them."

187.speaker: Lucian Galade
187.text: “First, the Supreme Court will no longer vote on constitutional amendments."

188.speaker: Lucian Galade
188.text: “The entire process will take a long time. But we must start working with a reform committee to evaluate all possibilities for a new Constitution as soon as possible.”

192.speaker: Lucian Galade
192.text: “We will form a reform committee together with all parties and start reaching out to all the stakeholders in the Assembly and the Court for a new Constitution."

193.speaker: Lucian Galade
193.text: “We will form a reform committee and start talking with all stakeholders in the Assembly and the Court to see if such changes to the Constitution would be possible."

194.speaker: Lucian Galade
194.text: “Let us at least work with a reform committee to start talking with all stakeholders in the Assembly and the Court just to query opinions. I'll try to reach out to the Old Guard, in the meantime."

195.speaker: Petr Vectern
195.text: "By later in the year, we should have an idea of the reform contents and what the other parties want."

196.speaker: Petr Vectern
196.text: "By later in the year, we should know more about the reform contents and how to balance the clauses of the new Constitution."

197.speaker: Petr Vectern
197.text: "By later in the year, we should have an idea about the reform contents and what the other parties want. Then we can decide whether to pull the trigger."

198.speaker: Player
198.text: “Our party must fall in line with our position. We can't have a strong divide."

199.speaker: Player
199.text: “The USP reformists aren't wrong to agree that we need change, but we should be in charge."

200.speaker: Petr Vectern
200.text: "We can't let the PFJP leadership take the spotlight on this."

201.speaker: Petr Vectern
201.text: "True. If our party fractures, it's the opposition that will benefit."

202.speaker: Player
202.text: “Mr. Ricter could be a potential ally in our goal to maintain a majority in the Assembly."

210.speaker: Player
210.text: “I won't be bought, it won't happen.”

211.speaker: Player
211.text: “I will enter a dialogue with them eventually. We need to be diplomatic.”

212.speaker: Lucian Galade
212.text: “However, to reform the constitution we must receive a two-thirds majority in the Grand National Assembly, which is 166 votes. *And* a simple majority in the Supreme Court that equates to 6 votes.”

213.speaker: Lucian Galade
213.text: “After we have settled on how to proceed, we will need to talk with our party figures. Our first goal must be to get the 150 signatures needed to start the process.”

217.speaker: Lucian Galade
217.text: “Talk to you soon, sir. I will keep in touch.”

218.speaker: Petr Vectern
218.text: “See you both at the next meeting.”

222.speaker: Lucian Galade
222.text: “True. But we can't let the Old Guard manipulate us and then backstab us, like we did with Alphonso."

227.speaker: Lucian Galade
227.text: “Frens Ricter, leader of the reformists, believes that true change can only be accomplished by transferring some of our powers to the Assembly. I will move into the details of their demands shortly."

228.speaker: Petr Vectern
228.text: “We did it Anton, we won! Finally! All those years with our noses to the grindstone paid off."

245.speaker: Lucian Galade
245.text: “Following the greenlight from the USP, we will reach out to the other party leaders to see if they would back our draft. The last step is to convince the justices of the Court.”

246.speaker: Narrator
246.text: Petr's eyes sparkled. The strain of the past months had put a damper on his usual rakish charm, but today he was looking and acting more like his old self. He loosened his tie and undid the top two buttons of his shirt.

247.speaker: Petr Vectern
247.text: "Enjoying the new secretary I picked out for you? Thought you'd appreciate her gorgeous set of... talents. It's a shame the rest of your staff aren't as easy on the eyes."

248.speaker: Narrator
248.text: He gestured to the slight paunch that protruded over his waistband.

249.speaker: Narrator
249.text: Lucian spoke in soft, clipped tones that immediately drew your attention towards what he had to say. Petr and I waited for him to proceed.

250.speaker: Petr Vectern
250.text: “We did it Anton, we won! Finally! The bribery, the backstabbing -- it's all paid off."

251.speaker: Petr Vectern
251.text: “We did it Anton, we won! Finally! All those games we played with the media paid off."

261.speaker: Lucian Galade
261.text: “Our election campaign promised to focus on the military. This was a safe choice. The military and the general staff are a powerful element in the state, and as history tells us, a dangerous one too.”

262.speaker: Lucian Galade
262.text: “The military and the general staff are a powerful element in the state, and as history tells us, a dangerous one too. We do have some room to make structural changes -- by reducing their budget, for example. But it is quite limited."

263.speaker: Player
263.text: “I want to work with them anyway. The new administration will be open to talk to businessmen.”

264.speaker: Player
264.text: “The military can be close allies. And with the Rumburg threat on the horizon, we need them.”

265.speaker: Player
265.text: “The Sordish Armed Forces represent our pride as a nation and will be funded as promised.”

266.speaker: Player
266.text: “With the Rumburg threat on the horizon, we can't reduce our defense capability and anger our General Staff.”

267.speaker: Player
267.text: “The military has been nothing but a burden on our society. We should do something drastic -- like cutting their funding.”

268.speaker: Player
268.text: “If they prove to be a political threat in the future, we can get rid of them.”

269.speaker: Lucian Galade
269.text: “Rumburg is a massive threat. One that also requires us to ally with other, stronger nations.”

270.speaker: Lucian Galade
270.text: “That will ensure they will be on our side unless we do something drastic in the course of our term.”

271.speaker: Lucian Galade
271.text: “I would advise the same. The budget should be maintained and we should refrain from confronting the military too directly.”

272.speaker: Lucian Galade
272.text: “That is possible, but we can be sure that there will be a strong negative reaction. If we push the military too far, it could cause real trouble.”

273.speaker: Lucian Galade
273.text: “Bold strategy Mr. President. One that could work, but we would need to amend the constitution first. Let's not get ahead of ourselves.”

274.speaker: Petr Vectern
274.text: “If we act strongly against the military, both of those guys will unite against us. I agree with Lucian. We need to tread carefully here."

275.speaker: Lucian Galade
275.text: “Defense Minister Iosef Lancea is more loyal to us compared to General Kruger. A fact that obviously can change with our actions. Either way, I see a potential rift between the two since they are clearly of different minds.”

276.speaker: Lucian Galade
276.text: “None of us want to live through the 1927 scenario again.”

277.speaker: Player
277.text: “I don't want to die in prison just like Artor S. Wisci did.”

278.speaker: Lucian Galade
278.text: “It is sound to listen to them but they have very biased and narrow opinions. Nationalism clouds their minds. General Kruger is a specter of the past.”

279.speaker: Player
279.text: “I want to receive the advice of the military before making up my mind.”

283.speaker: Player
283.text: “We won't let these privileged, greedy, and snobby capitalists run the country.”

284.speaker: Lucian Galade
284.text: “It's always easier for the administration to have businesses' support.”

285.speaker: Lucian Galade
285.text: “Alphonso said the same thing. I doubt there was anybody else to turn to in his case.”

286.speaker: Lucian Galade
286.text: “Wise approach. It's good to understand and see if we can reach a middle ground.”

287.speaker: Lucian Galade
287.text: “Let's not underestimate their influence. These are not harmless people either.”

288.speaker: Petr Vectern
288.text: “He'd be a useful ally as well. Tusk has an incredible network and owns a good amount of Bergia Steel.”

289.speaker: Player
289.text: “Tusk is heading the group. We should make sure he is on our side.”

291.speaker: Player
291.text: "That's exactly what I'm aiming to do."
